items: CBI is a non-statutory body established via an executive resolution in 1963, whereas NIA is a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament.
Under the 2019 amendment, NIA has extraterritorial jurisdiction to investigate offences committed against Indian citizens or interests outside India.
Superintendence over CBI regarding Prevention of Corruption Act cases vests with the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC), not DoPT.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) operates under the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT), whereas the National Investigation Agency (NIA) functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA).
CBI derives its police powers from the Delhi Special Police Establishment (DSPE) Act, 1946, while the NIA is a statutory body constituted under the National Investigation Agency Act, 2008.
CBI primary mandate includes corruption, economic offences, and complex multi-state crimes; NIA specializes exclusively in counter-terrorism and national security offences.
NIA possesses suo motu power to investigate terror-related cases nationwide without requiring state government consent.
CBI requires state consent (General or Specific) under Section 6 of the DSPE Act to investigate cases within a state's jurisdiction.
